o1.biggest_strength: Every recommendation traces to the owner's October numbers and the plan ranks by projected trials with a real Week 1 task list in Maya's words.
o1.biggest_mistake: Some projections stretch the data: ranking #1 rewrite /vs-google-analytics at 18-46 trials and the docs box estimate lean on CTR assumptions that are optimistic, and the plan spreads four writer slots over five moves in Month 1 when only four exist.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the trial projections to defensible ranges and make the Month 1 writer workload exactly four pages with no partial fifth.

o2.biggest_strength: Strong data table (trials per click, trials per page) and a sensible stop list that reframes reporting around trials by landing page.
o2.biggest_mistake: The headline '175 extra trials and 67 extra paid a month' is a full-ceiling fantasy that treats top-3 rankings as near-certain and overstates the return, plus the Month 2 'moving from GA4' page depends on an unverified product capability.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the ceiling math with probability-weighted, month-by-month trial forecasts and only propose pages the product can actually support.

reason: Output 1 reads like a plan I could hand the writer on Monday, keeps every projection anchored to my conversion rates, and gets the stop list and Week 1 right; Output 2 has good tables but sells me a 175-trial ceiling I don't believe and adds a page we may not be able to ship.
